why.WGMN: {topic} affects the quality of decisions, relationships and follow-through. In the WODDI Good Mother Network, volunteer leaders are often mothers, carers, traders, workers and community women who serve alongside family and work responsibilities, across different communities, mostly by phone. The goal is to turn this lesson into one observable behaviour: a clear decision, a helpful conversation, a documented action or a timely referral. Learn the principle before applying it; do not substitute enthusiasm for evidence or authority.
why.WNNN: {topic} affects the quality of decisions, relationships and follow-through. In the WODDI Nurture NextGen Network, volunteer leaders are young people aged 18 to 29: students, graduates, apprentices and early-career workers who balance classes, exams, first jobs and family expectations, and who connect mostly online. The goal is to turn this lesson into one observable behaviour: a clear decision, a helpful conversation, a documented action or a timely referral. Learn the principle before applying it; do not substitute enthusiasm for evidence or authority.

outcomes: By the end of this course you should be able to explain the five ideas in your own words, tell good practice from common mistakes, complete a practical activity and make a realistic improvement plan.
evidence: Learning evidence: record a dated example showing how you used {topic}. It can be a short reflection, a task record with no private details, or an action confirmed by your supervisor.
